exact_statement: Let C*>=0 and let f be Boolean with m>=2 relevant coordinates such that H(f_{i,s}) <= C* I(f_{i,s}) for every relevant i and s in {+1,-1}, and r=H(f)/I(f) > C*. Then for every relevant i: (a) Delta_i(f) >= C* Inf_i(f) + (r-C*) I(f) > r Inf_i(f); (b) B_i(f) > (r-2/ln 2) Inf_i(f) and Inf_i(f) < e^3 2^{-r}; (c) H(f)-B(f) <= (2/ln 2 - (m-1)(r-C*)) I(f) < (2/ln 2) I(f), so (m-1)(r-C*) <= 2/ln 2 and B(f)/H(f) > 1-2/(r ln 2). If some Boolean function violates H <= C* I, a violator with the fewest relevant variables exists and satisfies the hypotheses.

exact_statement: For every finite uniform Boolean sign f with n relevant variables, C>=0, delta=H(f)-CI(f), sigma_i=average_s(CI(f_i,s)-H(f_i,s)), and D=H-sum B_i, the exact signed identity D+(n-1)delta+sum sigma_i=sum JS_i holds. If delta>0 and all sigma_i>=0, then n>=2 and (n-1)(H/I-C)<=2/ln2. Therefore no diverging-relevant-dimension ratio-preserving Boolean embedding of a seed of ratio R>C can have all average one-coordinate children certified at that same C. If allowances C_m vary, C_m>=R_m-(2/ln2)/(n_m-1). For disjoint tensor powers, sigma_(copy,i)(f^tensor m)=sigma_i(f)-(m-1)(H(f)-CI(f)). For the three-bit point defect at C=8/3, m=2 loses individual but retains average child certification; m>=3 loses average certification. No Boolean function with n>=11 relevant inputs and ratio at least that seed ratio has all average children certified at C=8/3.
